sentence: The NHS says adults can take paracetamol and ibuprofen together if needed, but children should not be given them at the same time.
note: Paracetamol-adults page: adults can take paracetamol at the same time as ibuprofen if needed; NHS inform: can take both together if required; children: do not give at same time.

sentence: The NHS says adults can take paracetamol and ibuprofen at the same time if needed, and NHS inform says the two can be taken together if required.
note: Adults can take paracetamol at the same time as ibuprofen if needed; NHS inform: can take both together if required.

sentence: For children, the NHS says paracetamol and ibuprofen should not be given at the same time but one at a time.
note: Children: paracetamol can be given alongside ibuprofen but not at the same time; one at a time.

sentence: The NHS lists groups who should avoid ibuprofen or check first, including people with repeated stomach ulcers or bleeding, asthma, or severe kidney failure.
note: Who-can-and-cannot page: stomach bleeding/perforation/ulcer more than once; severe heart, kidney or liver failure; asthma, hay fever, allergies.

sentence: Many cold and flu products contain paracetamol or ibuprofen, so using several products can make it easy to take more than the recommended amount.
note: NHS inform: cough and cold medicines often contain paracetamol and ibuprofen so easy to take more than recommended dose.

sentence: The NHS says to call 999 for signs of a serious allergic reaction, and to get urgent advice from NHS 111 or a doctor for other serious effects such as stomach bleeding or kidney problems.
note: Side effects page: allergic reaction 999; stomach ulcers/bleeding and kidney problems 111 or doctor.

sentence: Ibuprofen belongs to a group of painkillers called non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, or NSAIDs.
note: Ibuprofen is an NSAID; ibuprofen, aspirin and naproxen belong to the same group.

sentence: The NHS describes ibuprofen as a painkiller that also treats inflammation.
note: Page title: painkiller that also treats inflammation.

sentence: It describes paracetamol as a painkiller for pain and high temperature.
note: Page title: painkiller for pain and high temperature.

sentence: For a dental abscess, NHS inform says ibuprofen is the preferred painkiller, and paracetamol can be taken instead if ibuprofen cannot be taken for medical reasons.
note: Dental abscess page: ibuprofen preferred; paracetamol if can't take it.

sentence: The NHS also says that if you need pain relief while taking warfarin, paracetamol is the one to take instead of ibuprofen.
note: Warfarin page: NSAIDs such as ibuprofen can affect anticoagulants (take paracetamol instead if you need pain relief).

sentence: For adults, the NHS says paracetamol can be taken at the same time as ibuprofen if needed.
note: Adults can take paracetamol at the same time as ibuprofen if needed.

sentence: It also says paracetamol can be taken with other painkillers that do not contain paracetamol, such as ibuprofen, aspirin or codeine.
note: Paracetamol with other painkillers that do not contain paracetamol, such as ibuprofen, aspirin or codeine.

sentence: NHS inform, the NHS information service for Scotland, also says the two can be taken together if required.
note: NHS inform: can take both together if required.

sentence: For a dental abscess, it says that if one painkiller does not work, taking both paracetamol and ibuprofen may help.
note: Dental abscess page: if one doesn't work, taking both may help.

sentence: The advice is different for children.
note: Children: cannot give both at the same time.

sentence: For them, the NHS says paracetamol can be given alongside ibuprofen but not at the same time, and the two should be given one at a time.
note: Children: not at the same time; one at a time.

sentence: The NHS lists several groups who should avoid ibuprofen or check with a professional before using it.
note: Who-can-and-cannot page lists exclusions.

sentence: These include people who have had an allergic reaction to aspirin or other NSAIDs, with signs such as wheezing, a runny nose or skin reactions.
note: Allergic reaction or symptoms like wheezing, runny nose or skin reactions after aspirin, ibuprofen or other NSAIDs.

sentence: They also include people who have had a hole in the stomach, bleeding in the stomach or a stomach ulcer more than once, and people with severe heart, kidney or liver failure.
note: Hole (perforation) in stomach, bleeding or ulcer more than once; severe heart, kidney or liver failure.

sentence: Asthma, hay fever and allergies are also on the NHS list.
note: Asthma, hay fever, or allergies listed.

sentence: The NHS also says to avoid ibuprofen in pregnancy unless a doctor or pharmacist advises it, and to check with a pharmacist or doctor when breastfeeding.
note: Avoid in pregnancy unless advised by doctor or pharmacist; breastfeeding check with pharmacist or doctor.

sentence: People over 65 are more likely to get stomach ulcers with ibuprofen, according to the NHS.
note: Over 65: ibuprofen can make stomach ulcers more likely.

sentence: Other medicines can interact with ibuprofen.
note: Ibuprofen can interact with some medicines.

sentence: The NHS interactions page lists warfarin and other anticoagulants, medicines for high blood pressure, steroids such as prednisolone, certain antibiotics and some antidepressants.
note: Page lists these as medicines that can interact with ibuprofen.

sentence: It advises against taking ginkgo biloba with ibuprofen because it can increase the chance of bleeding.
note: Advises against ginkgo biloba with ibuprofen; increases chance of bleeding.

sentence: For other herbal products, it says there is not enough information to say they are safe to take with ibuprofen.
note: Not enough information to say other herbal products are safe with ibuprofen.

sentence: NHS inform advises anyone already taking other medication to check with a pharmacist first.
note: Anyone already taking other medication should check with a pharmacist first.

sentence: Many cold and flu products contain paracetamol or ibuprofen.
note: Cough and cold medicines often contain paracetamol and ibuprofen.

sentence: NHS inform says this makes it easy to take more than the recommended dose.
note: Easy to take more than recommended dose.

sentence: The NHS says to avoid taking other medicines that contain paracetamol at the same time as paracetamol, such as cold and flu remedies, because too much can be dangerous.
note: Avoid paracetamol alongside other medicines containing paracetamol, e.g. cold and flu remedies; may take too much, which can be dangerous.

sentence: It adds that taking two different medicines that contain paracetamol carries a risk of overdose, and that too much paracetamol can sometimes damage the liver.
note: If you take 2 different medicines that contain paracetamol, risk of overdose; too much can sometimes damage your liver.

sentence: For ibuprofen, the NHS says to check the label of cold and cough remedies for aspirin, ibuprofen or other NSAIDs.
note: Check the label for aspirin, ibuprofen or other NSAIDs.

sentence: Taking ibuprofen with other NSAIDs such as aspirin or naproxen is not advised without speaking to a pharmacist or doctor, because side effects such as stomach ache become more likely.
note: Do not combine without speaking to pharmacist or doctor; may increase chance of side effects like stomach ache.

sentence: The NHS lists common side effects of ibuprofen as indigestion, stomach aches, feeling sick, being sick and headaches.
note: Common side effects listed.

sentence: Serious ones include stomach ulcers or bleeding in the stomach, and allergic reactions.
note: Stomach ulcers or bleeding; serious allergic reaction.

sentence: The NHS also lists kidney problems, such as swollen ankles or blood in the urine, as a reason to get urgent advice.
note: Kidney problems: swollen ankles, blood in pee; 111 or doctor.

sentence: For paracetamol, the NHS says there may be no obvious symptoms at first after taking too much, so feeling well does not rule out harm.
note: Often no obvious symptoms at first; contact 111 if you take too much even if you feel well.

sentence: For signs of a serious allergic reaction to ibuprofen, such as swollen lips, mouth, throat or tongue, fast or difficult breathing or a tight throat, the NHS says to call 999.
note: Allergic reaction signs: call 999.

sentence: The NHS also says to call 999 for severe chest or stomach pain, which can signal a hole in the stomach or gut, and for difficulty breathing or worsening asthma symptoms.
note: Severe chest or stomach pain, breathing trouble or worsening asthma: 999.

sentence: Vomiting blood or black, tar-like poo can be signs of bleeding in the stomach, and the NHS says to get urgent advice from NHS 111 or a doctor.
note: Stomach ulcers/bleeding with vomiting blood or black tar-like poo: 111 or doctor.

sentence: Swollen ankles or blood in the urine can point to a kidney problem, and the NHS says to contact NHS 111 or a doctor.
note: Kidney problems: 111 or doctor.

sentence: If too much paracetamol has been taken, the NHS says to contact NHS 111 for advice, even when the person feels well.
note: Contact 111 now if you take too much paracetamol, even if you feel well.

sentence: For questions that are not urgent, NHS inform says to speak to a pharmacist if unsure.
note: Speak to a pharmacist if you're unsure.
